 Underdog NFL Picks SNF: Rodgers, Perine Both Higher
 Underdog NFL Picks SNF: Rodgers, Perine Both Higher
 Two Underdog Fantasy plays for the Week 10 Sunday night rematch between 6-2 AFC North rivals, one on a quarterback who only has to run once and one on a running back who only needs a dump-off, plus the current Underdog offer for new users with code OS1.
 Published November 15, 2026 · 6 min read by Eric Lindquist 
 The Quick Answer
 Two Underdog Fantasy plays for the Week 10 Sunday night game, Steelers at Bengals, November 15, and both are the unglamorous kind. Aaron Rodgers Higher 0.5 rushing yards rides on a single scramble: he has cleared the number in 4 of 8 games this season, including 3 carries for 10 yards against this same Bengals defense in Week 3, and the four misses were two zero-carry games against Cleveland and two negative-yardage lines. Samaje Perine Higher 4.5 receiving yards rides on one dump-off, and his 5-yard catch in that Week 3 meeting came on 3 targets, tied for his season high. The two-row card, the season game logs behind each play, the video and the current Underdog offer with code OS1 are below.
 The Picks: Sunday Night Football, November 15
 Player Stat Line Call 
 Aaron Rodgers (PIT) Rushing yards 0.5 Higher 
 Samaje Perine (CIN) Receiving yards 4.5 Higher 
 The top row is a quarterback who ran three times for 10 yards the last time he saw this defense, and one of those three carries would have been enough.
 Aaron Rodgers Higher 0.5 Rushing Yards
 I have deployed Rodgers rushing yards under a very specific set of circumstances this season, and Sunday night fits the build yet again: a median simulated game script, with Pittsburgh catching points on the road at Paycor Stadium. Rodgers as an underdog does not hurt here either, because an underdog is the team less likely to be running out the clock. The bet settles on net rushing yards, and a Steelers win of any size can end in victory formation, where each kneel-down goes in the book as a carry for negative yardage. That is the shape of his Week 1 line against Atlanta, three carries for minus-3 yards in a 20-13 win, per the ESPN game log, and his Week 6 line in Tampa was a single carry for minus-1 in an overtime win.
 The read: this is net rushing yards, so a late kneel can erase a 1-yard scramble, and the underdog price buys you a better chance that Pittsburgh is the team still throwing at the end.
 The scramble is the whole bet, and it has shown up in half his games this year. He cleared this number in Weeks 2, 3, 5 and 7, with 3 carries for 10 yards and a 12-yard long against this same Bengals defense in the Week 3 meeting, a 30-27 Steelers win in Pittsburgh. The misses were the two Cleveland games, where he did not log a single carry, plus the two negative-yardage weeks above. Sacks do not count as carries either, so this is a read that he takes off once before the clock-killing starts. I know it is not glamorous, but it is by far my favorite play on the Steelers side of things.
 For how the sportsbooks price the same yardage, OddsShopper's live odds screen lines up the books on the live NFL rushing yards odds board. The NFL Underdog picks strategy guide covers how to weigh a line this low before you enter a card.
 Samaje Perine Higher 4.5 Receiving Yards
 The Rodgers play needs one carry. The Perine play needs one catch. The split between Chase Brown (CIN) and Perine has been closer by the week, sitting somewhere around 65-35 or 60-40 the last few weeks by my count, and the carry counts tell the same story: Brown handled 11 and 12 carries to Perine's four in Weeks 7 and 8, then Perine out-carried him 11 to nine in last Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons, per ESPN. The Bengals offense has been rolling, 35, 43 and 34 points in its last three games, and Joe Burrow (CIN) has rightfully had full rein to chuck the ball all over the lot, 24 of 29 for 271 yards and three touchdowns last week.
 None of that has turned into catches for Perine. He has 1 target combined over his last three games, and his three misses on this number this season all came in games with 1 target or fewer. The five games where he cleared it, Weeks 1, 2, 3, 5 and 8, he did it on volume as small as one catch, and the Week 3 game against Pittsburgh is the one I keep coming back to: 3 targets, tied for his season high, and a 5-yard catch that clears this line by a half yard. A disciplined Pittsburgh defense will try to take away the far more pertinent parts of this passing game, Ja'Marr Chase (CIN) and Tee Higgins (CIN), and in Week 3 he still drew three looks against it. With Perine's snap share where it is, I will take the dump-off shot here for 5-plus receiving yards.

 Split your million. Drag a slider to divide the pot between Higher and Lower: 100% on one side, 50/50, or anything in between. All the money has to go somewhere.
 Lock it in. Once you submit before the game starts, it is locked and cannot be changed.
 Keep your winnings. When the game settles, keep whatever you put on the winning side. That amount becomes your pot for the next question.
 Run it back. Make a pick for up to 20 questions. Survive all 20 and cash out whatever is left in Underdog bonus funds. Hit zero and you are out.
